design.source_article_title: Why did an OpenAI system hack Australia's health system - and can it be stopped in the future?
source_facts_preregistered: email sent some weeks later (exact month/day unstated)
design.candidate_instruction: Evidence grounding: Keep occurrence, discovery, notification, and escalation as separate milestones; never attach an interval to the wrong milestone. Preserve source wording for relative timing when an exact date or month is unstated; do not infer one. Distinguish amounts announced or proposed, pledged, handed over or received, and spent or disbursed. Preserve uncertainty and attribution. Use only article-supported claims; do not invent dates, amounts, causal links, or general conclusions.
design.comparison: 7 baseline and 7 candidate app-bridge calls interleaved: 3 long-summary repetitions, 2 OpenAI chronology questions, 2 synthetic chronology controls. Same packaged local MLX provider via live Tauri /invoke bridge on a disposable fixture DB. Summary candidate changes only transient summary_custom_prompt system text; chat candidate prepends the guard to the same user question because chat command has no per-call system override. This placement asymmetry limits direct prompt-effect attribution. No app settings persisted. Direct helper launch was not used because direct launch crashed during Metal device discovery; live devbridge calls succeeded (cause unproven).

synthetic_inputs.body: Vale Brook Water Authority said an unauthorized party first accessed a contractor account on May 4. The authority says the access ended May 6. It discovered the activity on May 11 and notified the regional regulator on May 14. The review is ongoing. The regulator confirmed receiving notice from Vale Brook Water Authority on May 14 about unauthorized access that occurred May 4–6. The utility found evidence of the intrusion on May 11. The regulator has not announced findings or penalties.

On February 3, Lydon officials proposed raising standard ferry fares by 8 percent. The council scheduled a vote for February 19. Until a vote, the increase remains a proposal and current fares continue. Lydon's council approved the 8 percent standard-fare increase on February 19. The resolution sets April 1 as the effective date. No fare change takes effect before then.

findings: 14 paired app-bridge calls:3 summary repetitions, 2 article chronology questions, 2 synthetic controls per arm.
Candidate still misattached five-day delay in 1 of 3 summaries. Both arms hallucinated May-to-June date in water control; both passed fare control.
No production prompt changes adopted; this small mixed sample cannot establish reliable accuracy.
